Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot and was seen for neck and upper back complaints
consistent with whiplash-type soft tissue injury. The reported mechanism of injury is in keeping with the pattern of symptoms
described at intake. Over the course of 28 visits, care proceeded along a conventional path, beginning with a period of more
frequent sessions focused on pain control, range-of-motion work, and graded strengthening. Visit frequency reduced steadily as
symptoms improved and the patient regained function. Examination findings included reduced cervical range of motion and
localized tenderness in the paraspinal muscles, which support the diagnosis. Some other orthopedic and neurological screening
tests were within normal limits. The patient also has a history of treatment to the same region within the past two years, and that
prior condition contributes to some of the current symptoms and limitations. Billing records reviewed for this episode show no
duplicate or repeated charges for the same services.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
